Our multilingual team (EN, AR, ES, DE) seeks members skilled to build innovative solutions using NASA data. Join us to create something extraordinary!
summary: TerraTwin is an Earth-analog intelligence platform designed to support research and planning for future lunar and Martian exploration. The project compares seven terrestrial analog sites: the Atacama Desert, Antarctica’s Dry Valleys, Haughton Crater, Death Valley, Iceland’s Rift Volcanics, Hawaiʻi’s Kīlauea region, and the Canadian Arctic. It organizes geological, thermal, topographic, and environmental data to examine similarities and differences between these Earth environments and the Moon and Mars. The platform presents these comparisons through an interactive website and a proposed analytical framework incorporating the Environmental Similarity Index (ESI), Integrated Feature Score (IFS), and Regolith and Mobility Hazard Index (RMHI). These indices are preliminary research tools and are not yet fully validated or intended as mission-certified standards. Claude and Gemini were used to support website development, ChatGPT contributed to project development, research organization, and refinement, and Gamma was used to create the presentation. The project emphasizes scientific references, measurement context, data limitations, and uncertainty, while identifying future improvements such as further source verification, dataset calibration, sensitivity analysis, and field validation. TerraTwin aims to make Earth-analog comparisons more accessible and systematic, supporting research into environments relevant to future lunar and Martian missions.
details: TerraTwin is an interactive research platform that explores how extreme environments on Earth can serve as terrestrial analogs for future Moon and Mars exploration. It examines seven selected locations: the Atacama Desert, Antarctica’s Dry Valleys, Haughton Crater, Death Valley, Iceland’s Rift Volcanic Regions, Hawaiʻi’s Kīlauea region, and the Canadian Arctic. The project organizes and compares scientific information across environmental, geological, thermal, and topographic characteristics to identify similarities and differences between these locations and extraterrestrial environments. It incorporates three preliminary research indices: the Environmental Similarity Index (ESI), the Integrated Feasibility Score (IFS), and the Resource and Mission Habitability Index (RMHI), providing a structured framework for comparative analysis. TerraTwin aims to make planetary analog research more accessible, organized, and understandable. Its potential benefits include supporting scientific exploration, helping researchers examine extreme terrestrial environments, and providing a comparative foundation for future lunar and Martian mission planning. The project combines an interactive website, a structured scientific research workbook, comparative data matrices, documented methodologies, and a GitHub repository. Its development and research process involved organizing scientific references, evaluating data quality, documenting limitations, and distinguishing verified measurements from unavailable or uncertain information. What makes TerraTwin distinctive is its integrated approach to comparing multiple extreme environments through a consistent research framework. The team considered scientific reliability, source traceability, environmental diversity, data limitations, and the importance of transparent comparisons. Its indices are preliminary research tools rather than validated mission standards or operational safety predictions.
